description: Curious minds, map lovers, and space geeks coming together to explore Earth's endless dance! We love turning complex data into cool visual stories and discovering what satellites can tell us about our ever-changing planet.
summary:
Belagavi is known as the sugar bowl of Karnataka, a state in India. As someone from Belagavi, I read about the sugarcane farmers' protests and their struggles almost every day. Sugarcane is a water-intensive crop, and with rainfall shortages and the effects of El Niño contributing to water scarcity in the region, using this precious resource efficiently becomes even more important for better yields. This made us explore soil moisture mapping, given its critical role in understanding the water needs of crops.

Soil moisture, vital for crop health and agricultural productivity, remains largely invisible to the human eye. By fusing NASA-ISRO NISAR satellite intelligence with the universal language of music, Pa-dha-ni-sar aims to make this information accessible. Its name creatively fuses Pa-Dha-Ni-Sa, the musical notes of Indian classical music, and NISAR, the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar mission, representing a meeting of India's musical heritage and space-based Earth observation.

Pa-dha-ni-sar transforms satellite-derived soil moisture information into an interactive musical experience, translating moisture variations into distinct musical tones. It brings the science of space closer to the everyday realities of farming, helping farmers hear the condition of their soil, understand their fields, and make more informed water management decisions. Our vision is to make the Earth speak through music.
details:
♫♪ Pa-dha-ni-sar ♩♬ — Rhythms of Earth (Acoustic Soil Moisture Insights)

Pa-dha-ni-sar is an interactive soil moisture mapping and data sonification application powered by NASA-ISRO NISAR satellite data. It enables farmers to explore the moisture conditions across their fields through a map-based interface and music.

The application translates satellite-derived soil moisture variations into distinct musical tones. Wetter regions produce Jaltarang-inspired notes, while drier regions produce low cello tones. Farmers can physically move through their fields and hear the changing moisture conditions around them. They can also explore the field from a bird's-eye view and listen to historical soil moisture patterns at a chosen location.

How does it work?

The farmer initiates a soil moisture measurement by clicking a button. The application uses the farmer's geographical location(lat, lon) and uses a default farm size to identify the corresponding farm region and retrieve NISAR Soil Moisture (SME2) data.

The farm area defaults to one hectare, and the historical period defaults to six months. Farmers can modify the farm size and select historical periods of one, three, or six months, or one year.

The backend processes the downloaded NISAR HDF5 files and extracts soil moisture information for the selected farm region. The resulting data is organized into a spatial grid, with latitude, longitude, moisture values, and corresponding dates stored in CSV files.

The application displays the farm on an interactive map, overlaid with the soil moisture grid. Farmers can switch between current and historical views.

As the farmer moves through the field, their location is represented by a moving dot or farmer icon. The moisture value associated with the corresponding grid cell is translated into a musical tone using data sonification based on soil moisture values. This interactive experience is inspired by the tile-based interactive floors found in museums, where movement across tiles produces different musical notes.

Farmers can also remain at a location and move the virtual marker across the field to explore moisture variations from a bird's-eye view of the field. Additionally, they can select a specific location and listen to its historical soil moisture patterns to understand how the spot has performed over time.

What benefits does it have?

Pa-dha-ni-sar makes satellite-derived soil moisture information more intuitive and engaging by introducing music as an alternative way to perceive geospatial data.

Intuitive interaction: Musical tones provide an accessible way to distinguish wetter and drier regions without relying entirely on numerical values or complex dashboards.

Field-level exploration: Farmers can interact with spatial moisture variations across their fields rather than viewing only a single aggregated value.

Historical understanding: Farmers can explore moisture patterns over time at specific locations to better understand changing soil conditions.

Water management: Soil moisture information can support more informed irrigation decisions and encourage efficient use of water, particularly for water-intensive crops such as sugarcane.

Accessible technology: The application aims to make satellite science easier to understand and interact with for farmers with varying levels of digital literacy. It bypasses literacy barriers and steep learning curves by leveraging human auditory processing instead of complex, text-heavy data charts.

Cost-Effective: Eliminates the need for expensive, high-maintenance on-ground IoT sensor networks. Provides instant geospatial insights without requiring technical training or manual soil-sampling tools.

What do we hope to achieve?

Our vision is to empower farmers facing severe water scarcity and yield pressures—particularly in critical agricultural hubs like Belagavi—to optimize irrigation for water-intensive crops like sugarcane.

We hope to extend this approach to different crops and agricultural regions. In the future, soil moisture information could be combined with Sentinel-2 NDVI, MODIS land-surface temperature, rainfall, and weather data to develop more comprehensive agricultural advisories.

Higher-resolution NISAR GCOV observations could also be explored for improved spatial detail, along with data alignment and fusion techniques to generate finer-grid moisture maps.

Ultimately, Pa-dha-ni-sar aims to bridge the gap between satellite observations and everyday farming decisions by transforming Earth observation data into an experience farmers can see, hear, and interact with. We want to make space-based Earth observation data deeply personal, engaging, and practically useful for everyday agricultural decisions.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software

Satellite data: NASA-ISRO NISAR Level 3 Soil Moisture (SME2) products, in HDF5 format.

Data discovery and retrieval: ASF Search Python library (`asf_search`).

Data processing: Python-based backend processing of HDF5 data and generation of spatial CSV datasets.

Data sonification: Musical tone mapping of soil moisture values, using Jaltarang-inspired tones for wetter regions and cello tones for drier regions.

Geospatial visualization: Interactive field map, spatial grid overlay, farmer location marker, and historical moisture visualization.

Hardware: Farmer's mobile device with location capability, such as GPS, for location-aware field interaction.
